title.narrative: Investing in Social Protection for Inclusion, Resilience, and Efficiency (INSPIRE) Project

description.narrative: The Additional Financing (AF) will bridge the reforms supported by the original INSPIRE project and other World Bank-financed operations with the next generation of Social Safety Net (SSN) reforms. It leverages the World Bank engagement in social protection sector in Ukraine, helping to sustain the provision of social benefits to over 2.6 million people during the war, enhancing existing systems and programs, and contributing to longer-term post-war recovery efforts. Twenty-nine types of benefits financed by the project provide social relief to low-income and energy-vulnerable households, vulnerable families, children, and students, as well as persons with disabilities. The AF will support structural improvements of the social assistance system to be achieved through (i) piloting a new Basic Income Benefit (BIB) program, which represents a major shift in social policy by combining various benefits into a single, efficient, shock-responsive, and inclusive program; (ii) further expanding the Guaranteed Minimum Income – Ukraine's main anti-poverty social assistance program - to support low-income families during the transition to the BIB; (iii) improving the administration of benefits; (iv) introducing rent subsidies and people-centric social services to strengthen support for Internally Displaced Persons; (v) and enhancing access to affordable childcare for vulnerable families. This comprehensive and cohesive reform package will help accelerate and scale up the modernization of the SSNs, paving the way for introducing the BIB program to significantly enhance support for vulnerable groups.

The development objective is to (i) contribute to sustaining the government's capacity to provide social support to the poor and vulnerable during the war: (ii) support the government's scale-up capacity to expand social support to the vulnerable during the war and beyond, and (iii) build a foundation for sustainable recovery by improving access to and quality of social and employment services for the poor and IDPs.

comment.narrative: PFU collects information on housing and utility costs from the service providers to strengthen administration of the energy assistance programs

title.narrative: The Borrower has completed verification of IDP assistance beneficiaries data using the UISSS to verify their compliance with the improved eligibility criteria for this type of social assistance

comment.narrative: In accordance with the Verification Protocols for PBCs, the PBC is achieved if, as on October 1, 2023, at least 50% of the recommendations provided by the MoF based on the results of the verification have been implemented by the structural units for social protection of the population. As on October 01, 2023, the structural subdivisions for social protection of the population have processed 129 827 recommendations, i.e. 71.61% of the total number of recommendations provided by the MoF as a result of the verification. The main factor that led to the cease of the social assistance for IDPs was the staying the person abroad for more than 30 calendar days in a row (58.1% of cease cases for IDP benefit).

title.narrative: The Borrower has enacted modifications to legislation to introduce means and assets testing to define eligibility for social assistance for IDPs to cover living expenses

comment.narrative: The MoSP introduced and implemented new IDP assistance that is based on means and asset testing that envisaged: (i) the shift from individual recipients to families—to introduce means testing considering the family's average per capita monthly income; (ii) cross-registry beneficiary verification at the enrollment stage using the public registries data; and (iii) maximum benefit duration of 12 months to discourage welfare dependency and facilitate self-sufficiency.
